content_html:
Introduction

F* (pronounced F star) is a general-purpose proof-oriented programming language, supporting both purely functional and effectful programming. It combines the expressive power of dependent types with proof automation based on SMT solving and tactic-based interactive theorem proving.

F* programs compile, by default, to OCaml. Various fragments of F* can also be extracted to F#, to C or Wasm by a tool called KaRaMeL, or to assembly using the Vale toolchain. F* is implemented in F* and bootstrapped using OCaml.

F* is open source on GitHub and is under active development by Microsoft Research, Inria, and by the community.

Download

F* is distributed under the Apache 2.0 license. Binaries for Windows, Linux, and Mac OS X are posted regularly on the releases page on GitHub. You can also install F* from OPAM, Docker, Nix, or build it from sources, by following the instructions in INSTALL.md.

Learn F*

An online book Proof-oriented Programming In F* is being written and regular updates are posted online. You probably want to read it while trying out examples and exercises in your browser by clicking the image below.

Low*

We also have a tutorial that covers Low*, a low-level subset of F*, which can be compiled to C by KaRaMeL.

Course Material

F* courses are often taught at various seasonal schools. Lectures and course materials for some of them are also a useful resource.

  • Embedding Proof-oriented Programming Languages in F*
    • Online lectures at the Oregon Programming Language Summer School (2021): Lecture notes, slides, code
  • Formal Verification with F* and Meta-F*
    • Lectures and tutorial at ECI 2019: Lecture notes, slides, code
  • Verifying Low-Level Code for Correctness and Security
    • Lectures at the Oregon Programming Language Summer School (2019): Lecture notes, slides, code
  • Program Verification with F*
    • Course at 2018 EUTypes Summer School, 8-12 August, 2018, Ohrid, Macedonia Course material

Community

Please use GitHub Discussions to ask questions about F*, learn about announcements, etc.

Although we previously used a Slack instance, we aim to consolidate our online community on this public forum on Zulip.

We also have a mailing list, which has very low traffic. You can subscribe at fstar-mailing-list.

The F* PoP Up Seminar, a users and developers meeting is open to all. We aim to schedule it once a month, though the schedule is irregular---we hope to see you there!

You can also contact the maintainers of F* at fstar-maintainers@googlegroups.com.

Uses

F* is used in several projects in both industrial and academic settings. We list a few of them here. If you are using F* in your project, please let us know by writing to the fstar-mailing-list.

Project Everest

Project Everest is an umbrella project that develops high-assurance secure communication software in F*. A big part of the development of F* has been motivated by the scenarios that Project Everest targets. Several offshoots from Project Everest continue as their own projects, including some of those listed below.

HACL*, ValeCrypt, and EverCrypt

HACL* is a library of high-assurance cryptographic primitives, written in F* and extracted to C. ValeCrypt provides formally proven implementations of cryptographic primitives in Vale, a framework for verified assembly language programming embedded in F*. EverCrypt combines them into a single cryptographic provider. Code from these projects is now used in production in several projects, including Mozilla Firefox, the Linux kernel, Python, mbedTLS, the Tezos blockchain, the ElectionGuard electronic voting SDK, and the Wireguard VPN.

EverParse

EverParse is a parser generator for binary formats that produces C code extracted from formally proven F*. Parsers from EverParse are used in production in several projects, including in Windows Hyper-V, where every network packet passing through the Azure cloud platform is parsed and validated first by code generated by EverParse. EverParse is also used in other production settings, including ebpf-for-windows.

Research

F* is an active topic of research, both in the programming languages and formal methods community, as well as from an application perspective in the security and systems communities. We list a few of them below, with full citations to these papers available in this bibliography. If you would like your paper included in this list, please contact fstar-maintainers@googlegroups.com.

The Design of F* and its DSLs

  • Dependent Types and Multi-monadic Effects in F* (POPL 2016) This is the canonical reference describing the F* system. The language has evolved in significant ways since 2016, however, its core design and implementation is based on this paper.
  • Verified Low-level Programming Embedded in F* (ICFP 2017) which describes the Low* fragment of F* which is a low-level subset of F* that can be compiled to C by KaRaMeL.
  • A Verified, Efficient Embedding of a Verifiable Assembly Language (POPL 2019) which describes the Vale language, a verified assembly language embedded in F*.
  • Meta-F*: Proof Automation with SMT, Tactics, and Metaprograms (ESOP 2019) which describes MetaF*, a metaprogramming system within F* used to implement various aspects of F*, ranging from its tactic engine to its support for typeclasses.
  • Programming and Proving with Indexed Effects (TR 2021) which describes the design of F*'s support for user-defined effects and provides a calculus that describes the logical core of F*.
  • Steel: Proof-oriented Programming in a Dependently Typed Concurrent Separation Logic (ICFP 2021), which describes the Steel language and its use of the SteelCore concurrent separation logic for proofs of imperative programs with various forms of concurrency.

Semantics and Effects

  • Verifying Higher-order Programs with the Dijkstra Monad (PLDI 2013), which introduces the concept of the Dijkstra monad, a core feature of F*'s system of effects.
  • Dijkstra Monads for Free (POPL 2017), which shows how to automatically derive Dijkstra monads for a class of computational monads using a continuation-passing transformation
  • A Monadic Framework for Relational Verification: Applied to Information Security, Program Equivalence, and Optimizations (CPP 2018), which builds on the Dijkstra Monads for Free work to construct a framework for proving properties that relate multiple programs or program executions.
  • Dijkstra Monads for All (ICFP 2019), which generalizes the notion of a Dijkstra monad and shows how to systematically relate computational and specificational monads via monad morphisms.
  • Recalling a Witness: Foundations and Applications of Monotonic State (POPL 2018), which describes the design of a program logic for reasoning about programs whose state evolves monotonically, e.g., where the state is an append-only log. This logic underpins both Low* and Steel.
  • SteelCore: An Extensible Concurrent Separation Logic for Effectful Dependently Typed Programs (ICFP 2020), which describes the SteelCore concurrent separation logic, the basis of the Steel DSL.
  • USSL: A Universe-Stratified, Predicative Concurrent Separation Logic a foundational, axiom-free concurrent separation logic shallowly embedded in F*, supporting dynamic invariants and higher-order ghost state in a predicative setting, by stratifying predicates according to the hierarchy of universe levels.
  • PulseCore: An Impredicative Concurrent Separation Logic for Dependently Typed Programs (PLDI 2025), a foundational, axiom-free concurrent separation logic shallowly embedded in F*, supporting dynamic invariants and higher-order ghost state, with impredicative invariants and later credits. PulseCore is the foundation for Pulse, an embedded language in F* for proof-oriented programming in concurrent separation logic.

Applications in Security and Cryptography

Many papers applying F* in security and cryptography can be found in the Project Everest bibliography. We mention a few prominent ones here as well as other applications not related to Project Everest.

  • WYS*: A DSL for Verified Secure Multi-party Computations (POST 2017), which describes the WYS* language, a domain-specific language for writing verified mixed-mode secure multi-party computations.
  • Implementing and Proving the TLS 1.3 Record Layer(S&P 2017), which describes a verified implementaion of the TLS-1.3 record layer in Low*.
  • HACL*: A Verified Modern Cryptographic Library (CCS 2017), which describes HACL*, a verified cryptographic library implemented in Low*.
  • Formally Verified Cryptographic Web Applications in WebAssembly (S&P 2019), which develops LibSignal*, an implementation of the Signal protocol in F* using HACL*, compiled to Wasm by KaRaMeL.
  • EverCrypt: A Fast, Verified, Cross-Platform Cryptographic Provider (S&P 2020), a crypto provider combining C and assembly code from HACL* and Vale, as well as some applications built on top of it, including a verified high-performance Merkle tree that was used in an initial version of Microsoft Azure CCF.
  • HACL×N: Verified Generic SIMD Crypto (for all your favorite platforms) (CCS 2020), which metaprograms vectorized versions of cryptographic primitives, enabling a "write-once, get vectorized versions for free" style.
  • A Security Model and Fully Verified Implementation for the IETF QUIC Record Layer (S&P 2021), a verified implementation of the QUIC record layer in Low* combined with the protocol logic implemented in Dafny.
  • DICE*: A Formally Verified Implementation of DICE Measured Boot (USENIX Security 2021), which proves the correctness & security of the DICE measured boot protocol for micro-controllers, implemented in Low*, using EverCrypt and EverParse.
  • DY*: A Modular Symbolic Verification Framework for Executable Cryptographic Protocol Code (Euro S&P 2021), a framework for type-based symbolic security analysis of cryptographic protocol implementations developed in F*.
  • A Tutorial-Style Introduction to DY* (LNCS 2021), which is, yes, a tutorial-style introduction to DY*.
  • An In-Depth Symbolic Security Analysis of the ACME Standard (CCS 2021), which proves the security of a model of the ACME certificate issuance and management protocol using DY*.
  • Noise*: A Library of Verified High-Performance Secure Channel Protocol Implementations (S&P 2022), which metaprograms provably secure implementations for a family of secure channel protocols.
  • TreeSync: Authenticated Group Management for Messaging Layer Security (USENIX Security 2023), a reference implementation of MLS in F*, proven secure using the DY* framework.
  • Modularity, Code Specialization, and Zero-Cost Abstractions for Program Verification (ICFP 2023), which describes proof-engineering techniques used in HACL* for generic implementations of cryptographic constructions that can be specialized repeatedly to many concrete implementations in C. The techniques used here led to the adoption of verified cryptographic code into the libraries of the Python programming language.
  • Verifying Indistinguishability of Privacy-Preserving Protocols (OOPSLA 2023), which provides a library called Waldo in F* that enables proofs of indistinguishability over traces of communication in networking protocols.
  • Comparse: Provably Secure Formats for Cryptographic Protocols (CCS 2023), which provides a parsing library for data formats that are appropriate for use with symbolic protocol analyzers. Comparse provides bit-level precise accounting of formats allowing the DY* protocol analysis framework to reason about concrete messages and identify protocol flaws that it previously would have missed.
  • Formal Security and Functional Verification of Cryptographic Protocol Implementations in Rust (CCS 2025), which develops Bert13, an implementation of TLS-1.3 in Rust with post-quantum features, and proves it correct and secure via translation (using Hax) to a variety of prover backends, including F*, which is used to prove the Rust code panic free and to prove that the transcript formats are injective.

Applications in Systems

  • Provably-Safe Multilingual Software Sandboxing using WebAssembly (USENIX 2022), which describes a verified implementation of a sandbox for WebAssembly modules in Low* and Rust.
  • FastVer: Making Data Integrity a Commodity (SIGMOD 2021), which formalizes a protocol for data integrity monitoring in F*.
  • FastVer2: A Provably Correct Monitor for Concurrent, Key-Value Stores (CPP 2022), which proves the correctness of a low-level, concurrent implementation of the FastVer protocol in Steel.
  • Pipit on the Post: Proving Pre- and Post-Conditions of Reactive Systems (ECOOP 2024), which embeds a reactive language in F* and uses it to verify some control systems that execute in real time.
  • StarMalloc: Verifying a Modern, Hardened Memory Allocator (SPLASH 2024), a security-oriented, concurrent memory allocator that can be used as a drop-in replacement in real-world projects, verified in Steel.

Applications in Parsing

  • EverParse: Verified Secure Zero-Copy Parsers for Authenticated Message Formats (USENIX Security 2019), which describes the EverParse parser generator for parsing binary formats, producing C code.
  • Hardening Attack Surfaces with Formally Proven Binary Format Parsers (PLDI 2022), which uses EverParse to harden network packet parsers in Windows Network Virtualization and Hyper-V.
  • ASN1*: Provably Correct Non-Malleable Parsing for ASN.1 DER (CPP 2022), which formalizes the ASN.1 DER format in F* and proves the correctness of a parser for it in EverParse.
  • Secure Parsing and Serializing with Separation Logic Applied to CBOR, CDDL, and COSE (CCS 2025), which formalizes the RFCs for the CBOR binary object format and the CDDL data description language in F*, develops provably correct and secure parsers and formatters for CBOR, and a compiler for CDDL specifications, all implemented in Pulse, and applied to various applications, including the validation of COSE signed objects.

Applications in Programming, Program Proof, and Program Analysis

  • Verified Compilation of Space-Efficient Reversible Circuits (CAV 2018), which presents ReVerC, a compiler for reversible circuits proven correct in F*.
  • Verified Transformations and Hoare Logic: Beautiful Proofs for Ugly Assembly Language (VSTTE 2020), which develops verified transformations for assembly programs in the Vale framework.
  • Statically verified refinements for multiparty protocols (OOPSLA 2020), which presents Session*, a session-typed programming language for multiparty protocols, formalized in F*.
  • Verified Functional Programming of an Abstract Interpreter (SAS 2021), which develops an abstract interpretation framework for an imperative language with a very compact proof of soundness developed in F*.
  • Catala: a programming language for the law (ICFP 2021), where core parts of the compiler are formalized and proven correct in F*.
  • Verification of a Merkle Patricia Tree Library Using F*, which ports a Merkle tree library from OCaml to F*, finds and fixes a bug, and eventually proves it correct.
  • Certified mergeable replicated data types (PLDI 2022), which presents PEEPUL, a framework in which to build replicated data types for use in distributed programming, formalized in F*.
  • Aeneas: Rust verification by functional translation (ICFP 2022), which translates Rust into pure F* enabling functional correctness proofs.
  • Q*: Implementing Quantum Separation Logic in F* (PlanQC 2022), which adapts the SteelCore separation logic for use with a quantum programming language.
  • Pipit: Reactive Systems in F* (Extended Abstract) (TyDe 2023), which describes a embedded DSL for verifying reactive systems.
  • Securing Verified IO Programs Against Unverified Code in F* (POPL 2024), which presents SCIO*, a formally secure compilation framework for statically verified programs performing input-output (IO).
  • SecRef*: Securely Sharing Mutable References between Verified and Unverified Code in F* (ICFP 2025), which presents SecRef*, a formally secure compilation framework for statically verified stateful programs. It also presents a Dijkstra Monad for Monotonic State.
  • Automatically Verifying Replication-Aware Linearizability (OOPSLA 2025), which develops a novel fully automated technique for verifying replication-aware linearizability for Mergeable Replicated Data Types, with proofs in F*, and verified code extracted to OCaml.
  • A Mechanically Verified Garbage Collector for OCaml (JAR 2025), which develops a verified stop-the-world mark-and-sweep GC for OCaml, verified in F* and Low*.

AI-assisted Programming

  • Towards Neural Synthesis for SMT-Assisted Proof-Oriented Programming (ICSE 2025), which curates a dataset of 940KLOC of F* code and proof and develops AI models to automate program and proof synthesis
  • 3DGen: AI-Assisted Generation of Provably Correct Binary Format Parsers, which developsAI agents to transform mixed informal input, including natural language documents (i.e., RFCs) and example inputs into format specifications into 3D, a data format specification language used with EverParse.

Miscellaneous

  • A Theorem Proving Approach to Programming Language Semantics (ICSE-SEET 2023), which reports on experiences teaching operational, denotational, and axiomatic semantics to students using F*.

Papers about an older version of F*

The first paper to introduce a system called F* was in 2011. Although the current version of F* was redesigned and implemented in 2015, we include some of these older papers here for completeness.

  • Secure Distributed Programming with Value-dependent Types (ICFP 2011), a longer version of which also appeared in JFP.
  • Self-certification: bootstrapping certified typecheckers in F* with Coq (POPL 2012), which certifies the correctness of the F* typechecker by programming it in F* itself and bootstrapping the process by checking about 7GB of proof using Coq in about 24 machine-days of compute time.
  • Fully abstract compilation to JavaScript (POPL 2013), which models a subset of JavaScript in F* and develops a secure compiler from an ML-like language to JavaScript.
  • Gradual typing embedded securely in JavaScript (POPL 2014), which develops a source-to-source compiler for JavaScript with defensive checks to ensure the soundness of gradual typing in adversarial contexts, proven corrent in F*.
  • Probabilistic relational verification for cryptographic implementations (POPL 2014), which develops RF*, a relational dialect of the language useful for proving security properties like noninterference and for game-based cryptographic proofs.

sentences.zh: USSSL：宇宙分层、谓词并发分离逻辑 一种浅层嵌入 F* 中的基础、无公理并发分离逻辑，通过根据宇宙级别的层次结构对谓词进行分层，支持谓词设置中的动态不变量和高阶幽灵状态。

blocks.html_en: • PulseCore: An Impredicative Concurrent Separation Logic for Dependently Typed Programs (PLDI 2025), a foundational, axiom-free concurrent separation logic shallowly embedded in F*, supporting dynamic invariants and higher-order ghost state, with impredicative invariants and later credits. PulseCore is the foundation for Pulse, an embedded language in F* for proof-oriented programming in concurrent separation logic.

sentences.en: PulseCore: An Impredicative Concurrent Separation Logic for Dependently Typed Programs (PLDI 2025), a foundational, axiom-free concurrent separation logic shallowly embedded in F*, supporting dynamic invariants and higher-order ghost state, with impredicative invariants and later credits.
sentences.zh: PulseCore：用于依赖类型程序的命令式并发分离逻辑（PLDI 2025），浅层嵌入 F* 中的基础、无公理并发分离逻辑，支持动态不变量和高阶幽灵状态，具有命令式不变量和后来的学分。

sentences.en: PulseCore is the foundation for Pulse, an embedded language in F* for proof-oriented programming in concurrent separation logic.
sentences.zh: PulseCore 是 Pulse 的基础，Pulse 是 F* 中的一种嵌入式语言，用于并发分离逻辑中面向证明的编程。

blocks.html_en: Applications in Security and Cryptography

sentences.en: Applications in Security and Cryptography
sentences.zh: 安全和密码学中的应用

blocks.html_en: Many papers applying F* in security and cryptography can be found in the Project Everest bibliography. We mention a few prominent ones here as well as other applications not related to Project Everest.

sentences.en: Many papers applying F* in security and cryptography can be found in the Project Everest bibliography.
sentences.zh: 在珠穆朗玛峰项目参考书目中可以找到许多在安全和密码学中应用 F* 的论文。

sentences.en: We mention a few prominent ones here as well as other applications not related to Project Everest.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里提到了一些突出的应用程序以及与珠穆朗玛峰项目无关的其他应用程序。

blocks.html_en: • WYS*: A DSL for Verified Secure Multi-party Computations (POST 2017), which describes the WYS* language, a domain-specific language for writing verified mixed-mode secure multi-party computations.

sentences.en: WYS*: A DSL for Verified Secure Multi-party Computations (POST 2017), which describes the WYS* language, a domain-specific language for writing verified mixed-mode secure multi-party computations.
sentences.zh: WYS*：用于经过验证的安全多方计算的 DSL (POST 2017)，它描述了 WYS* 语言，这是一种用于编写经过验证的混合模式安全多方计算的领域特定语言。

blocks.html_en: • Implementing and Proving the TLS 1.3 Record Layer(S&P 2017), which describes a verified implementaion of the TLS-1.3 record layer in Low*.

sentences.en: Implementing and Proving the TLS 1.3 Record Layer(S&P 2017), which describes a verified implementaion of the TLS-1.3 record layer in Low*.
sentences.zh: 实现和证明 TLS 1.3 记录层（S&P 2017），描述了 Low* 中经过验证的 TLS-1.3 记录层实现。

blocks.html_en: • HACL*: A Verified Modern Cryptographic Library (CCS 2017), which describes HACL*, a verified cryptographic library implemented in Low*.

sentences.en: HACL*: A Verified Modern Cryptographic Library (CCS 2017), which describes HACL*, a verified cryptographic library implemented in Low*.
sentences.zh: HACL*：经过验证的现代密码库 (CCS 2017)，它描述了 HACL*，这是一个在 Low* 中实现的经过验证的密码库。

blocks.html_en: • Formally Verified Cryptographic Web Applications in WebAssembly (S&P 2019), which develops LibSignal*, an implementation of the Signal protocol in F* using HACL*, compiled to Wasm by KaRaMeL.

sentences.en: Formally Verified Cryptographic Web Applications in WebAssembly (S&P 2019), which develops LibSignal*, an implementation of the Signal protocol in F* using HACL*, compiled to Wasm by KaRaMeL.
sentences.zh: WebAssembly 中经过正式验证的加密 Web 应用程序 (S&P 2019)，它开发了 LibSignal*，这是使用 HACL* 在 F* 中实现 Signal 协议的方法，由 KaRaMeL 编译为 Wasm。

blocks.html_en: • EverCrypt: A Fast, Verified, Cross-Platform Cryptographic Provider (S&P 2020), a crypto provider combining C and assembly code from HACL* and Vale, as well as some applications built on top of it, including a verified high-performance Merkle tree that was used in an initial version of Microsoft Azure CCF.

sentences.en: EverCrypt: A Fast, Verified, Cross-Platform Cryptographic Provider (S&P 2020), a crypto provider combining C and assembly code from HACL* and Vale, as well as some applications built on top of it, including a verified high-performance Merkle tree that was used in an initial version of Microsoft Azure CCF.
sentences.zh: EverCrypt：快速、经过验证的跨平台加密提供程序 (S&P 2020)，这是一个结合了 HACL* 和 Vale 的 C 和汇编代码的加密提供程序，以及在其之上构建的一些应用程序，包括在 Microsoft Azure CCF 初始版本中使用的经过验证的高性能 Merkle 树。

blocks.html_en: • HACL×N: Verified Generic SIMD Crypto (for all your favorite platforms) (CCS 2020), which metaprograms vectorized versions of cryptographic primitives, enabling a "write-once, get vectorized versions for free" style.

sentences.en: HACL×N: Verified Generic SIMD Crypto (for all your favorite platforms) (CCS 2020), which metaprograms vectorized versions of cryptographic primitives, enabling a "write-once, get vectorized versions for free" style.
sentences.zh: HACL×N：经过验证的通用 SIMD 加密（适用于所有您喜欢的平台）（CCS 2020），它对加密原语的矢量化版本进行元编程，从而实现“一次写入，免费获取矢量化版本”的风格。

blocks.html_en: • A Security Model and Fully Verified Implementation for the IETF QUIC Record Layer (S&P 2021), a verified implementation of the QUIC record layer in Low* combined with the protocol logic implemented in Dafny.

sentences.en: A Security Model and Fully Verified Implementation for the IETF QUIC Record Layer (S&P 2021), a verified implementation of the QUIC record layer in Low* combined with the protocol logic implemented in Dafny.
sentences.zh: IETF QUIC 记录层的安全模型和完全验证的实现 (S&P 2021)，Low* 中 QUIC 记录层的验证实现与 Dafny 中实现的协议逻辑相结合。

blocks.html_en: • DICE*: A Formally Verified Implementation of DICE Measured Boot (USENIX Security 2021), which proves the correctness & security of the DICE measured boot protocol for micro-controllers, implemented in Low*, using EverCrypt and EverParse.

sentences.en: DICE*: A Formally Verified Implementation of DICE Measured Boot (USENIX Security 2021), which proves the correctness & security of the DICE measured boot protocol for micro-controllers, implemented in Low*, using EverCrypt and EverParse.
sentences.zh: DICE*：DICE 测量启动的正式验证实现（USENIX Security 2021），证明了微控制器 DICE 测量启动协议的正确性和安全性，使用 EverCrypt 和 EverParse 在 Low* 中实现。

blocks.html_en: • DY*: A Modular Symbolic Verification Framework for Executable Cryptographic Protocol Code (Euro S&P 2021), a framework for type-based symbolic security analysis of cryptographic protocol implementations developed in F*.

sentences.en: DY*: A Modular Symbolic Verification Framework for Executable Cryptographic Protocol Code (Euro S&P 2021), a framework for type-based symbolic security analysis of cryptographic protocol implementations developed in F*.
sentences.zh: DY*：可执行加密协议代码的模块化符号验证框架（Euro S&P 2021），是在 F* 中开发的用于对加密协议实现进行基于类型的符号安全分析的框架。

blocks.html_en: • A Tutorial-Style Introduction to DY* (LNCS 2021), which is, yes, a tutorial-style introduction to DY*.

sentences.en: A Tutorial-Style Introduction to DY* (LNCS 2021), which is, yes, a tutorial-style introduction to DY*.
sentences.zh: DY* 教程式介绍 (LNCS 2021)，是的，DY* 教程式介绍。

blocks.html_en: • An In-Depth Symbolic Security Analysis of the ACME Standard (CCS 2021), which proves the security of a model of the ACME certificate issuance and management protocol using DY*.

sentences.en: An In-Depth Symbolic Security Analysis of the ACME Standard (CCS 2021), which proves the security of a model of the ACME certificate issuance and management protocol using DY*.
sentences.zh: ACME 标准 (CCS 2021) 的深入符号安全分析，证明了使用 DY* 的 ACME 证书颁发和管理协议模型的安全性。

blocks.html_en: • Noise*: A Library of Verified High-Performance Secure Channel Protocol Implementations (S&P 2022), which metaprograms provably secure implementations for a family of secure channel protocols.

sentences.en: Noise*: A Library of Verified High-Performance Secure Channel Protocol Implementations (S&P 2022), which metaprograms provably secure implementations for a family of secure channel protocols.
sentences.zh: Noise*：经过验证的高性能安全通道协议实现库 (S&P 2022)，它对一系列安全通道协议的可证明安全的实现进行元编程。

blocks.html_en: • TreeSync: Authenticated Group Management for Messaging Layer Security (USENIX Security 2023), a reference implementation of MLS in F*, proven secure using the DY* framework.

sentences.en: TreeSync: Authenticated Group Management for Messaging Layer Security (USENIX Security 2023), a reference implementation of MLS in F*, proven secure using the DY* framework.
sentences.zh: TreeSync：消息传递层安全性的经过身份验证的组管理 (USENIX Security 2023)，F* 中 MLS 的参考实现，使用 DY* 框架证明是安全的。

blocks.html_en: • Modularity, Code Specialization, and Zero-Cost Abstractions for Program Verification (ICFP 2023), which describes proof-engineering techniques used in HACL* for generic implementations of cryptographic constructions that can be specialized repeatedly to many concrete implementations in C. The techniques used here led to the adoption of verified cryptographic code into the libraries of the Python programming language.

sentences.en: Modularity, Code Specialization, and Zero-Cost Abstractions for Program Verification (ICFP 2023), which describes proof-engineering techniques used in HACL* for generic implementations of cryptographic constructions that can be specialized repeatedly to many concrete implementations in C.
sentences.zh: Modularity, Code Specialization, and Zero-Cost Abstractions for Program Verification (ICFP 2023)，描述了 HACL* 中使用的证明工程技术，用于加密结构的通用实现，这些加密结构可以重复专门化为 C 中的许多具体实现。

sentences.en: The techniques used here led to the adoption of verified cryptographic code into the libraries of the Python programming language.
sentences.zh: 这里使用的技术使得经过验证的加密代码被采用到 Python 编程语言的库中。

blocks.html_en: • Verifying Indistinguishability of Privacy-Preserving Protocols (OOPSLA 2023), which provides a library called Waldo in F* that enables proofs of indistinguishability over traces of communication in networking protocols.

sentences.en: Verifying Indistinguishability of Privacy-Preserving Protocols (OOPSLA 2023), which provides a library called Waldo in F* that enables proofs of indistinguishability over traces of communication in networking protocols.
sentences.zh: 验证隐私保护协议的不可区分性 (OOPSLA 2023)，它提供了一个名为 Waldo in F* 的库，可以证明网络协议中通信痕迹的不可区分性。

blocks.html_en: • Comparse: Provably Secure Formats for Cryptographic Protocols (CCS 2023), which provides a parsing library for data formats that are appropriate for use with symbolic protocol analyzers. Comparse provides bit-level precise accounting of formats allowing the DY* protocol analysis framework to reason about concrete messages and identify protocol flaws that it previously would have missed.

sentences.en: Comparse: Provably Secure Formats for Cryptographic Protocols (CCS 2023), which provides a parsing library for data formats that are appropriate for use with symbolic protocol analyzers.
sentences.zh: Comparse：可证明安全的加密协议格式 (CCS 2023)，它提供了适合符号协议分析器使用的数据格式的解析库。

sentences.en: Comparse provides bit-level precise accounting of formats allowing the DY* protocol analysis framework to reason about concrete messages and identify protocol flaws that it previously would have missed.
sentences.zh: Comparse 提供位级精确的格式计算，允许 DY* 协议分析框架推理具体消息并识别以前可能遗漏的协议缺陷。

blocks.html_en: • Formal Security and Functional Verification of Cryptographic Protocol Implementations in Rust (CCS 2025), which develops Bert13, an implementation of TLS-1.3 in Rust with post-quantum features, and proves it correct and secure via translation (using Hax) to a variety of prover backends, including F*, which is used to prove the Rust code panic free and to prove that the transcript formats are injective.

sentences.en: Formal Security and Functional Verification of Cryptographic Protocol Implementations in Rust (CCS 2025), which develops Bert13, an implementation of TLS-1.3 in Rust with post-quantum features, and proves it correct and secure via translation (using Hax) to a variety of prover backends, including F*, which is used to prove the Rust code panic free and to prove that the transcript formats are injective.
sentences.zh: Rust 中加密协议实现的形式安全性和功能验证 (CCS 2025)，开发了 Bert13，这是 Rust 中具有后量子功能的 TLS-1.3 实现，并通过翻译（使用 Hax）到各种证明者后端（包括 F*）来证明其正确性和安全性，其中 F* 用于证明 Rust 代码无恐慌，并证明转录格式是单射的。

blocks.html_en: Applications in Systems

sentences.en: Applications in Systems
sentences.zh: 系统应用

blocks.html_en: • Provably-Safe Multilingual Software Sandboxing using WebAssembly (USENIX 2022), which describes a verified implementation of a sandbox for WebAssembly modules in Low* and Rust.

sentences.en: Provably-Safe Multilingual Software Sandboxing using WebAssembly (USENIX 2022), which describes a verified implementation of a sandbox for WebAssembly modules in Low* and Rust.
sentences.zh: 使用 WebAssembly 的可证明安全的多语言软件沙箱 (USENIX 2022)，它描述了 Low* 和 Rust 中 WebAssembly 模块沙箱的经过验证的实现。

blocks.html_en: • FastVer: Making Data Integrity a Commodity (SIGMOD 2021), which formalizes a protocol for data integrity monitoring in F*.

sentences.en: FastVer: Making Data Integrity a Commodity (SIGMOD 2021), which formalizes a protocol for data integrity monitoring in F*.
sentences.zh: FastVer：使数据完整性成为商品 (SIGMOD 2021)，它正式确定了 F* 中数据完整性监控的协议。

blocks.html_en: • FastVer2: A Provably Correct Monitor for Concurrent, Key-Value Stores (CPP 2022), which proves the correctness of a low-level, concurrent implementation of the FastVer protocol in Steel.

sentences.en: FastVer2: A Provably Correct Monitor for Concurrent, Key-Value Stores (CPP 2022), which proves the correctness of a low-level, concurrent implementation of the FastVer protocol in Steel.
sentences.zh: FastVer2：可证明正确的并发键值存储监视器 (CPP 2022)，它证明了 Steel 中 FastVer 协议的低级并发实现的正确性。

blocks.html_en: • Pipit on the Post: Proving Pre- and Post-Conditions of Reactive Systems (ECOOP 2024), which embeds a reactive language in F* and uses it to verify some control systems that execute in real time.

sentences.en: Pipit on the Post: Proving Pre- and Post-Conditions of Reactive Systems (ECOOP 2024), which embeds a reactive language in F* and uses it to verify some control systems that execute in real time.
sentences.zh: Pipit on the Post: Proving Pre-and Post-Conditions of Reactive Systems (ECOOP 2024)，在 F* 中嵌入了反应式语言，并用它来验证一些实时执行的控制系统。

blocks.html_en: • StarMalloc: Verifying a Modern, Hardened Memory Allocator (SPLASH 2024), a security-oriented, concurrent memory allocator that can be used as a drop-in replacement in real-world projects, verified in Steel.

sentences.en: StarMalloc: Verifying a Modern, Hardened Memory Allocator (SPLASH 2024), a security-oriented, concurrent memory allocator that can be used as a drop-in replacement in real-world projects, verified in Steel.
sentences.zh: StarMalloc：验证现代的、强化的内存分配器 (SPLASH 2024)，一种面向安全的并发内存分配器，可用作实际项目中的直接替代品，已在 Steel 中进行验证。

blocks.html_en: Applications in Parsing

sentences.en: Applications in Parsing
sentences.zh: 解析中的应用

blocks.html_en: • EverParse: Verified Secure Zero-Copy Parsers for Authenticated Message Formats (USENIX Security 2019), which describes the EverParse parser generator for parsing binary formats, producing C code.

sentences.en: EverParse: Verified Secure Zero-Copy Parsers for Authenticated Message Formats (USENIX Security 2019), which describes the EverParse parser generator for parsing binary formats, producing C code.
sentences.zh: EverParse: Verified Secure Zero-Copy Parsers for Authenticated Message Formats (USENIX Security 2019)，它描述了用于解析二进制格式、生成 C 代码的 EverParse 解析器生成器。

blocks.html_en: • Hardening Attack Surfaces with Formally Proven Binary Format Parsers (PLDI 2022), which uses EverParse to harden network packet parsers in Windows Network Virtualization and Hyper-V.

sentences.en: Hardening Attack Surfaces with Formally Proven Binary Format Parsers (PLDI 2022), which uses EverParse to harden network packet parsers in Windows Network Virtualization and Hyper-V.
sentences.zh: 使用经过正式验证的二进制格式解析器强化攻击面 (PLDI 2022)，它使用 EverParse 强化 Windows 网络虚拟化和 Hyper-V 中的网络数据包解析器。

blocks.html_en: • ASN1*: Provably Correct Non-Malleable Parsing for ASN.1 DER (CPP 2022), which formalizes the ASN.1 DER format in F* and proves the correctness of a parser for it in EverParse.

sentences.en: ASN1*: Provably Correct Non-Malleable Parsing for ASN.1 DER (CPP 2022), which formalizes the ASN.1 DER format in F* and proves the correctness of a parser for it in EverParse.
sentences.zh: ASN1*：Provously Correct Non-Malleable Parsing for ASN.1 DER (CPP 2022)，它以 F* 形式化了 ASN.1 DER 格式，并证明了 EverParse 中解析器的正确性。

blocks.html_en: • Secure Parsing and Serializing with Separation Logic Applied to CBOR, CDDL, and COSE (CCS 2025), which formalizes the RFCs for the CBOR binary object format and the CDDL data description language in F*, develops provably correct and secure parsers and formatters for CBOR, and a compiler for CDDL specifications, all implemented in Pulse, and applied to various applications, including the validation of COSE signed objects.

sentences.en: Secure Parsing and Serializing with Separation Logic Applied to CBOR, CDDL, and COSE (CCS 2025), which formalizes the RFCs for the CBOR binary object format and the CDDL data description language in F*, develops provably correct and secure parsers and formatters for CBOR, and a compiler for CDDL specifications, all implemented in Pulse, and applied to various applications, including the validation of COSE signed objects.
sentences.zh: 使用分离逻辑进行安全解析和序列化应用于 CBOR、CDDL 和 COSE (CCS 2025)，它将 CBOR 二进制对象格式的 RFC 和 F* 中的 CDDL 数据描述语言形式化，为 CBOR 开发可证明正确且安全的解析器和格式化程序，以及 CDDL 规范的编译器，所有这些都在 Pulse 中实现，并应用于各种应用程序，包括 COSE 签名对象的验证。

blocks.html_en: Applications in Programming, Program Proof, and Program Analysis

sentences.en: Applications in Programming, Program Proof, and Program Analysis
sentences.zh: 在编程、程序证明和程序分析中的应用

blocks.html_en: • Verified Compilation of Space-Efficient Reversible Circuits (CAV 2018), which presents ReVerC, a compiler for reversible circuits proven correct in F*.

sentences.en: Verified Compilation of Space-Efficient Reversible Circuits (CAV 2018), which presents ReVerC, a compiler for reversible circuits proven correct in F*.
sentences.zh: Verified Compilation of Space-Efficient Reversible Circuits (CAV 2018)，其中介绍了 ReVerC，这是一种在 F* 中被证明正确的可逆电路编译器。

blocks.html_en: • Verified Transformations and Hoare Logic: Beautiful Proofs for Ugly Assembly Language (VSTTE 2020), which develops verified transformations for assembly programs in the Vale framework.

sentences.en: Verified Transformations and Hoare Logic: Beautiful Proofs for Ugly Assembly Language (VSTTE 2020), which develops verified transformations for assembly programs in the Vale framework.
sentences.zh: Verified Transformations and Hoare Logic: Beautiful Proofs for Ugly Assembly Language (VSTTE 2020)，它为 Vale 框架中的汇编程序开发了经过验证的转换。

blocks.html_en: • Statically verified refinements for multiparty protocols (OOPSLA 2020), which presents Session*, a session-typed programming language for multiparty protocols, formalized in F*.

sentences.en: Statically verified refinements for multiparty protocols (OOPSLA 2020), which presents Session*, a session-typed programming language for multiparty protocols, formalized in F*.
sentences.zh: 多方协议的静态验证改进 (OOPSLA 2020)，其中提出了 Session*，一种用于多方协议的会话类型编程语言，以 F* 形式化。

blocks.html_en: • Verified Functional Programming of an Abstract Interpreter (SAS 2021), which develops an abstract interpretation framework for an imperative language with a very compact proof of soundness developed in F*.

sentences.en: Verified Functional Programming of an Abstract Interpreter (SAS 2021), which develops an abstract interpretation framework for an imperative language with a very compact proof of soundness developed in F*.
sentences.zh: 抽象解释器的验证函数式编程 (SAS 2021)，它为命令式语言开发了一个抽象解释框架，并具有在 F* 中开发的非常紧凑的健全性证明。

blocks.html_en: • Catala: a programming language for the law (ICFP 2021), where core parts of the compiler are formalized and proven correct in F*.

sentences.en: Catala: a programming language for the law (ICFP 2021), where core parts of the compiler are formalized and proven correct in F*.
sentences.zh: Catala：一种法律编程语言（ICFP 2021），其中编译器的核心部分在 F* 中被形式化并被证明是正确的。

blocks.html_en: • Verification of a Merkle Patricia Tree Library Using F*, which ports a Merkle tree library from OCaml to F*, finds and fixes a bug, and eventually proves it correct.

sentences.en: Verification of a Merkle Patricia Tree Library Using F*, which ports a Merkle tree library from OCaml to F*, finds and fixes a bug, and eventually proves it correct.
sentences.zh: 使用 F* 验证 Merkle Patricia 树库，将 Merkle 树库从 OCaml 移植到 F*，发现并修复错误，并最终证明其正确。

blocks.html_en: • Certified mergeable replicated data types (PLDI 2022), which presents PEEPUL, a framework in which to build replicated data types for use in distributed programming, formalized in F*.

sentences.en: Certified mergeable replicated data types (PLDI 2022), which presents PEEPUL, a framework in which to build replicated data types for use in distributed programming, formalized in F*.
sentences.zh: 经过认证的可合并复制数据类型 (PLDI 2022)，它提出了 PEEPUL，这是一个构建用于分布式编程的复制数据类型的框架，以 F* 形式化。

blocks.html_en: • Aeneas: Rust verification by functional translation (ICFP 2022), which translates Rust into pure F* enabling functional correctness proofs.

sentences.en: Aeneas: Rust verification by functional translation (ICFP 2022), which translates Rust into pure F* enabling functional correctness proofs.
sentences.zh: Aeneas：通过功能翻译进行 Rust 验证 (ICFP 2022)，它将 Rust 翻译为纯 F*，从而实现功能正确性证明。

blocks.html_en: • Q*: Implementing Quantum Separation Logic in F* (PlanQC 2022), which adapts the SteelCore separation logic for use with a quantum programming language.

sentences.en: Q*: Implementing Quantum Separation Logic in F* (PlanQC 2022), which adapts the SteelCore separation logic for use with a quantum programming language.
sentences.zh: Q*：在 F* 中实现量子分离逻辑（PlanQC 2022），它采用了 SteelCore 分离逻辑以与量子编程语言一起使用。

blocks.html_en: • Pipit: Reactive Systems in F* (Extended Abstract) (TyDe 2023), which describes a embedded DSL for verifying reactive systems.

sentences.en: Pipit: Reactive Systems in F* (Extended Abstract) (TyDe 2023), which describes a embedded DSL for verifying reactive systems.
sentences.zh: Pipit：F* 中的反应式系统（扩展摘要）（TyDe 2023），描述了用于验证反应式系统的嵌入式 DSL。

blocks.html_en: • Securing Verified IO Programs Against Unverified Code in F* (POPL 2024), which presents SCIO*, a formally secure compilation framework for statically verified programs performing input-output (IO).

sentences.en: Securing Verified IO Programs Against Unverified Code in F* (POPL 2024), which presents SCIO*, a formally secure compilation framework for statically verified programs performing input-output (IO).

content_html_zh:
介绍

F*（发音为 F star）是一种通用的面向证明的编程语言，支持纯函数式和有效的编程。 它将依赖类型的表达能力与基于 SMT 求解和基于策略的交互式定理证明的证明自动化相结合。

默认情况下，F* 程序编译为 OCaml。 F* 的各种片段还可以通过 KaRaMeL 工具提取为 F#、C 或 Wasm，或者使用 Vale 工具链进行汇编。 F* 在 F* 中实现并使用 OCaml 进行引导。

F* 在 GitHub 上开源，并由 Microsoft Research、Inria 和社区积极开发。

下载

F* 在 Apache 2.0 许可证下分发。 Windows、Linux 和 Mac OS X 的二进制文件定期发布在 GitHub 的发布页面上。 您还可以按照 INSTALL.md 中的说明从 OPAM、Docker、Nix 安装 F*，或从源代码构建它。

学习F*

正在编写一本在线书《Proof-orientated Planning In F*》，并定期更新在线发布。 您可能想通过单击下图在浏览器中尝试示例和练习的同时阅读它。

Low*

我们还有一个涵盖 Low* 的教程，它是 F* 的低级子集，可以通过 KaRaMeL 编译为 C。

课程资料

F* 课程通常在各种季节性学校教授。 其中一些人的讲座和课程材料也是有用的资源。

  • 在 F* 中嵌入面向证明的编程语言 俄勒冈州编程语言暑期学校在线讲座（2021 年）：讲义、幻灯片、代码
  • ECI 2019 上的 F* 和 Meta-F* 形式化验证讲座和教程：讲稿、幻灯片、代码
  • 验证低级代码的正确性和安全性 俄勒冈编程语言暑期学校讲座（2019）：讲义、幻灯片、代码
  • 2018 年 EUTypes 暑期学校 F* 课程项目验证，2018 年 8 月 8 日至 12 日，马其顿奥赫里德 课程材料

社区

请使用 GitHub 讨论区提出有关 F* 的问题、了解公告等。

尽管我们之前使用过 Slack 实例，但我们的目标是在 Zulip 的这个公共论坛上巩固我们的在线社区。

我们还有一个邮件列表，其流量非常低。 您可以在 fstar-mailing-list 订阅。

F* PoP Up 研讨会是一个向所有人开放的用户和开发者会议。 我们的目标是每月安排一次，尽管日程安排不固定——我们希望在那里见到您！

您还可以通过 fstar-maintainers@googlegroups.com 联系 F* 的维护者。

Uses

F* 用于工业和学术环境中的多个项目。 我们在这里列出其中的一些。 如果您在项目中使用 F*，请写信至 fstar-mailing-list 告知我们。

珠穆朗玛峰计划

Project Everest 是一个在 F* 中开发高保证安全通信软件的伞式项目。 F* 开发的很大一部分是由珠穆朗玛峰项目的目标场景推动的。 珠穆朗玛峰计划的几个分支继续作为自己的项目，包括下面列出的一些项目。

HACL*、ValeCrypt 和 EverCrypt

HACL* 是一个高可信度加密原语库，用 F* 编写并提取到 C。 ValeCrypt 在 Vale 中提供经过正式验证的加密原语实现，Vale 是一个嵌入 F* 中的经过验证的汇编语言编程框架。 EverCrypt 将它们组合成一个单一的加密提供程序。 这些项目的代码现已在多个项目的生产中使用，包括 Mozilla Firefox、Linux 内核、Python、mbedTLS、Tezos 区块链、ElectionGuard 电子投票 SDK 和 Wireguard VPN。

永远解析

EverParse 是一个二进制格式的解析器生成器，可生成从经过形式验证的 F* 中提取的 C 代码。 EverParse 的解析器在多个项目的生产中使用，包括在 Windows Hyper-V 中，其中通过 Azure 云平台的每个网络数据包首先由 EverParse 生成的代码进行解析和验证。 EverParse 还用于其他生产环境，包括 ebpf-for-windows。

研究

无论是在编程语言和形式方法社区，还是从安全和系统社区的应用程序角度来看，F* 都是一个活跃的研究主题。 我们在下面列出了其中的一些，并在本参考书目中提供了这些论文的完整引用。 如果您希望您的论文包含在此列表中，请联系 fstar-maintainers@googlegroups.com。

F*及其DSL的设计

  • F* 中的依赖类型和多元效应 (POPL 2016) 这是描述 F* 系统的规范参考。 自 2016 年以来，该语言已经发生了重大发展，但其核心设计和实现都是基于本文的。
  • 经过验证的嵌入 F* 中的低级编程 (ICFP 2017)，它描述了 F* 的 Low* 片段，它是 F* 的低级子集，可以通过 KaRaMeL 编译为 C。
  • 可验证汇编语言的经验证、高效嵌入 (POPL 2019) 描述了 Vale 语言，这是一种嵌入 F* 中的经过验证的汇编语言。
  • Meta-F*：使用 SMT、策略和元程序进行证明自动化 (ESOP 2019)，它描述了 MetaF*，F* 中的元编程系统，用于实现 F* 的各个方面，从策略引擎到对类型类的支持。
  • 使用索引效果进行编程和证明 (TR 2021)，描述了 F* 支持用户定义效果的设计，并提供了描述 F* 逻辑核心的微积分。
  • Steel：依赖类型并发分离逻辑中的面向证明编程 (ICFP 2021)，它描述了 Steel 语言及其使用 SteelCore 并发分离逻辑来证明具有各种并发形式的命令式程序。

语义和效果

  • 使用 Dijkstra Monad 验证高阶程序 (PLDI 2013)，介绍了 Dijkstra Monad 的概念，这是 F* 效果系统的核心特征。
  • Dijkstra Monads for Free (POPL 2017)，展示了如何使用连续传递变换自动导出一类计算 monads 的 Dijkstra Monads
  • A Monadic Framework for Relational Verification: Applied to Information Security, Program Equivalence, and Optimizations (CPP 2018)，它建立在 Dijkstra Monads for Free 工作的基础上，构建一个用于证明与多个程序或程序执行相关的属性的框架。
  • Dijkstra Monads for All (ICFP 2019)，概括了 Dijkstra monad 的概念，并展示了如何通过 monad 态射系统地将计算和规范 monad 联系起来。
  • 回忆见证：单调状态的基础和应用 (POPL 2018)，它描述了用于推理状态单调演变的程序的程序逻辑设计，例如，状态是仅附加日志的情况。 这一逻辑是 Low* 和 Steel 的基础。
  • SteelCore: An Extensible Concurrent Separation Logic for Effectful Dependly Typed Programs (ICFP 2020)，它描述了 SteelCore 并发分离逻辑，这是 Steel DSL 的基础。
  • USSSL：宇宙分层、谓词并发分离逻辑 一种浅层嵌入 F* 中的基础、无公理并发分离逻辑，通过根据宇宙级别的层次结构对谓词进行分层，支持谓词设置中的动态不变量和高阶幽灵状态。
  • PulseCore：用于依赖类型程序的命令式并发分离逻辑（PLDI 2025），浅层嵌入 F* 中的基础、无公理并发分离逻辑，支持动态不变量和高阶幽灵状态，具有命令式不变量和后来的学分。 PulseCore 是 Pulse 的基础，Pulse 是 F* 中的一种嵌入式语言，用于并发分离逻辑中面向证明的编程。

安全和密码学中的应用

在珠穆朗玛峰项目参考书目中可以找到许多在安全和密码学中应用 F* 的论文。 我们在这里提到了一些突出的应用程序以及与珠穆朗玛峰项目无关的其他应用程序。

  • WYS*：用于经过验证的安全多方计算的 DSL (POST 2017)，它描述了 WYS* 语言，这是一种用于编写经过验证的混合模式安全多方计算的领域特定语言。
  • 实现和证明 TLS 1.3 记录层（S&P 2017），描述了 Low* 中经过验证的 TLS-1.3 记录层实现。
  • HACL*：经过验证的现代密码库 (CCS 2017)，它描述了 HACL*，这是一个在 Low* 中实现的经过验证的密码库。
  • WebAssembly 中经过正式验证的加密 Web 应用程序 (S&P 2019)，它开发了 LibSignal*，这是使用 HACL* 在 F* 中实现 Signal 协议的方法，由 KaRaMeL 编译为 Wasm。
  • EverCrypt：快速、经过验证的跨平台加密提供程序 (S&P 2020)，这是一个结合了 HACL* 和 Vale 的 C 和汇编代码的加密提供程序，以及在其之上构建的一些应用程序，包括在 Microsoft Azure CCF 初始版本中使用的经过验证的高性能 Merkle 树。
  • HACL×N：经过验证的通用 SIMD 加密（适用于所有您喜欢的平台）（CCS 2020），它对加密原语的矢量化版本进行元编程，从而实现“一次写入，免费获取矢量化版本”的风格。
  • IETF QUIC 记录层的安全模型和完全验证的实现 (S&P 2021)，Low* 中 QUIC 记录层的验证实现与 Dafny 中实现的协议逻辑相结合。
  • DICE*：DICE 测量启动的正式验证实现（USENIX Security 2021），证明了微控制器 DICE 测量启动协议的正确性和安全性，使用 EverCrypt 和 EverParse 在 Low* 中实现。
  • DY*：可执行加密协议代码的模块化符号验证框架（Euro S&P 2021），是在 F* 中开发的用于对加密协议实现进行基于类型的符号安全分析的框架。
  • DY* 教程式介绍 (LNCS 2021)，是的，DY* 教程式介绍。
  • ACME 标准 (CCS 2021) 的深入符号安全分析，证明了使用 DY* 的 ACME 证书颁发和管理协议模型的安全性。
  • Noise*：经过验证的高性能安全通道协议实现库 (S&P 2022)，它对一系列安全通道协议的可证明安全的实现进行元编程。
  • TreeSync：消息传递层安全性的经过身份验证的组管理 (USENIX Security 2023)，F* 中 MLS 的参考实现，使用 DY* 框架证明是安全的。
  • Modularity, Code Specialization, and Zero-Cost Abstractions for Program Verification (ICFP 2023)，描述了 HACL* 中使用的证明工程技术，用于加密结构的通用实现，这些加密结构可以重复专门化为 C 中的许多具体实现。 这里使用的技术使得经过验证的加密代码被采用到 Python 编程语言的库中。
  • 验证隐私保护协议的不可区分性 (OOPSLA 2023)，它提供了一个名为 Waldo in F* 的库，可以证明网络协议中通信痕迹的不可区分性。
  • Comparse：可证明安全的加密协议格式 (CCS 2023)，它提供了适合符号协议分析器使用的数据格式的解析库。 Comparse 提供位级精确的格式计算，允许 DY* 协议分析框架推理具体消息并识别以前可能遗漏的协议缺陷。
  • Rust 中加密协议实现的形式安全性和功能验证 (CCS 2025)，开发了 Bert13，这是 Rust 中具有后量子功能的 TLS-1.3 实现，并通过翻译（使用 Hax）到各种证明者后端（包括 F*）来证明其正确性和安全性，其中 F* 用于证明 Rust 代码无恐慌，并证明转录格式是单射的。

系统应用

  • 使用 WebAssembly 的可证明安全的多语言软件沙箱 (USENIX 2022)，它描述了 Low* 和 Rust 中 WebAssembly 模块沙箱的经过验证的实现。
  • FastVer：使数据完整性成为商品 (SIGMOD 2021)，它正式确定了 F* 中数据完整性监控的协议。
  • FastVer2：可证明正确的并发键值存储监视器 (CPP 2022)，它证明了 Steel 中 FastVer 协议的低级并发实现的正确性。
  • Pipit on the Post: Proving Pre-and Post-Conditions of Reactive Systems (ECOOP 2024)，在 F* 中嵌入了反应式语言，并用它来验证一些实时执行的控制系统。
  • StarMalloc：验证现代的、强化的内存分配器 (SPLASH 2024)，一种面向安全的并发内存分配器，可用作实际项目中的直接替代品，已在 Steel 中进行验证。

解析中的应用

  • EverParse: Verified Secure Zero-Copy Parsers for Authenticated Message Formats (USENIX Security 2019)，它描述了用于解析二进制格式、生成 C 代码的 EverParse 解析器生成器。
  • 使用经过正式验证的二进制格式解析器强化攻击面 (PLDI 2022)，它使用 EverParse 强化 Windows 网络虚拟化和 Hyper-V 中的网络数据包解析器。
  • ASN1*：Provously Correct Non-Malleable Parsing for ASN.1 DER (CPP 2022)，它以 F* 形式化了 ASN.1 DER 格式，并证明了 EverParse 中解析器的正确性。
  • 使用分离逻辑进行安全解析和序列化应用于 CBOR、CDDL 和 COSE (CCS 2025)，它将 CBOR 二进制对象格式的 RFC 和 F* 中的 CDDL 数据描述语言形式化，为 CBOR 开发可证明正确且安全的解析器和格式化程序，以及 CDDL 规范的编译器，所有这些都在 Pulse 中实现，并应用于各种应用程序，包括 COSE 签名对象的验证。

在编程、程序证明和程序分析中的应用

  • Verified Compilation of Space-Efficient Reversible Circuits (CAV 2018)，其中介绍了 ReVerC，这是一种在 F* 中被证明正确的可逆电路编译器。
  • Verified Transformations and Hoare Logic: Beautiful Proofs for Ugly Assembly Language (VSTTE 2020)，它为 Vale 框架中的汇编程序开发了经过验证的转换。
  • 多方协议的静态验证改进 (OOPSLA 2020)，其中提出了 Session*，一种用于多方协议的会话类型编程语言，以 F* 形式化。
  • 抽象解释器的验证函数式编程 (SAS 2021)，它为命令式语言开发了一个抽象解释框架，并具有在 F* 中开发的非常紧凑的健全性证明。
  • Catala：一种法律编程语言（ICFP 2021），其中编译器的核心部分在 F* 中被形式化并被证明是正确的。
  • 使用 F* 验证 Merkle Patricia 树库，将 Merkle 树库从 OCaml 移植到 F*，发现并修复错误，并最终证明其正确。
  • 经过认证的可合并复制数据类型 (PLDI 2022)，它提出了 PEEPUL，这是一个构建用于分布式编程的复制数据类型的框架，以 F* 形式化。
  • Aeneas：通过功能翻译进行 Rust 验证 (ICFP 2022)，它将 Rust 翻译为纯 F*，从而实现功能正确性证明。
  • Q*：在 F* 中实现量子分离逻辑（PlanQC 2022），它采用了 SteelCore 分离逻辑以与量子编程语言一起使用。
  • Pipit：F* 中的反应式系统（扩展摘要）（TyDe 2023），描述了用于验证反应式系统的嵌入式 DSL。
  • 保护经过验证的 IO 程序免受 F* 中未经验证的代码的影响 (POPL 2024)，其中介绍了 SCIO*，这是一种正式的安全编译框架，用于执行输入输出 (IO) 的静态验证程序。
  • SecRef*：在 F* 中已验证和未验证代码之间安全地共享可变引用 (ICFP 2025)，其中介绍了 SecRef*，这是一种用于静态验证有状态程序的形式安全编译框架。 它还提出了单调状态的 Dijkstra Monad。
  • 自动验证复制感知线性化 (OOPSLA 2025)，开发了一种新颖的全自动技术，用于验证可合并复制数据类型的复制感知线性化，并使用 F* 进行证明，并验证提取到 OCaml 的代码。
  • A Mechanically Verified Garbage Collector for OCaml (JAR 2025)，为 OCaml 开发了经过验证的停止世界标记和清除 GC，并在 F* 和 Low* 中进行了验证。

AI辅助编程

  • Towards Neural Synthesis for SMT-Assisted Proof-Oriented Planning (ICSE 2025)，该项目策划了 940KLOC 的 F* 代码和证明数据集，并开发了 AI 模型来自动化程序和证明合成
  • 3DGen：AI 辅助生成可证明正确的二进制格式解析器，它开发 AI 代理来将混合的非正式输入（包括自然语言文档（即 RFC）和示例输入）转换为 3D（一种与 EverParse 一起使用的数据格式规范语言）。

各种各样的

  • 编程语言语义的定理证明方法 (ICSE-SEET 2023)，报告了使用 F* 向学生教授操作、指称和公理语义的经验。

关于旧版本 F* 的论文

第一篇介绍 F* 系统的论文发表于 2011 年。 尽管 F* 的当前版本是在 2015 年重新设计和实现的，但为了完整性，我们在此处包含了一些较旧的论文。

  • 具有值相关类型的安全分布式编程 (ICFP 2011)，其较长版本也出现在 JFP 中。
  • 自我认证：使用 Coq 在 F* 中引导经过认证的类型检查器（POPL 2012），通过在 F* 本身中进行编程来证明 F* 类型检查器的正确性，并通过使用 Coq 在大约 24 个机器日的计算时间内检查大约 7GB 的证明来引导该过程。
  • 对 JavaScript 的完全抽象编译 (POPL 2013)，它在 F* 中对 JavaScript 的子集进行建模，并开发了从类 ML 语言到 JavaScript 的安全编译器。
  • 安全嵌入 JavaScript 中的渐进式打字 (POPL 2014)，它为 JavaScript 开发了一个源到源的编译器，具有防御性检查，以确保对抗性上下文中渐进式打字的健全性，在 F* 中已被证明是正确的。
  • 密码实现的概率关系验证 (POPL 2014)，它开发了 RF*，这是一种语言的关系方言，可用于证明无干扰等安全属性和基于游戏的密码证明。
